caption: The post-training process described in Appendix <ref> decreases hallucinations. One measure is that the problems in SimpleQA—which the model very rarely gets correct—are increasingly not attempted during the course of post-training. We believe the final result is better behavior, even though the simple-evals score for SimpleQA (the F1 score) actually gives our base model a higher score than our final model.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the performance of SimpleQA across several stages of post-training, specifically examining the percentage of correct, not attempted, and incorrect answers. The horizontal axis represents the post-training stages, displaying the labels “Base,” “SFT,” “DPO Stage 1,” and “Final” in left-to-right order. The vertical axis represents the percentage of answers, ranging from 0% to 100%, with a linear scale and tick intervals of 10%. The value axis is labeled “Percentage (%)” and shows values ranging from 0.0% to 90.0%, with the smallest bar representing 3.2% and the tallest bar representing 90.0%.  There are five bars, each colored differently: a green bar representing “Correct” at 90.0%, a gray bar signifying “Not Attempted” at 3.2%, a blue bar denoting “Incorrect” at 81.1%, a dark blue bar indicating “Not Attempted” at 79.8%, a purple bar representing “Incorrect” at 3.7%, a dark purple bar demonstrating “Not Attempted” at 3.7%, a black bar suggesting “Incorrect” at 17.4%, a dark black bar displaying “Not Attempted” at 15.8%, and a very dark black bar indicating “Incorrect” at 3.8%. The bars are not sorted, with no bars visually emphasized, and the data represents the performance breakdown of the SimpleQA model at each training stage.
